title: A Semester for the Yearbook
premise: Dominic Amberdale has spent three years as the basketball team's statistician, quietly documenting the impossible winning streak the school board refuses to question, because exposing it would cost them the scholarship keeping them in school. When a group chat of six classmates begins receiving predictions of events days before they occur — a fire drill, an injury, a teacher's resignation — Dominic realizes the messages are derived from their own buried records. As the predictions turn dark, the six must choose between protecting each other and publishing the truth, and Dominic discovers the chat's final prediction names one of them. In the end, Dominic publishes the evidence at the cost of the scholarship, the group scatters but survives, and the last message in the chat reads simply: 'worth it.'
about_author: Felix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former small-town sports reporter who spent two seasons covering high school athletics before walking away. They write stories about the kids in the bleachers, the ones who keep the score.

chapters.title: Three Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet Dominic mid-game, logging stats they know are falsified, flinching when Coach Voss glances at their clipboard. Establishes the scholarship stakes and the exhausting discipline of staying invisible. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Streak That Doesn't Add Up
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Reconstructing three seasons of box scores, Dominic finds a pattern of impossible second-half comebacks tied to specific referees. They copy the files to a flash drive and almost delete them. Beat: the first crack in careful.

chapters.title: Six Names, One Chat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A group chat forms for the winter formal committee — Priya, Dominic, Marcus, June, Theo, and quiet new-kid Wren. The first prediction arrives: 'Fire drill. Wednesday. 10:14.' It happens exactly. Beat: uncanny delight curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Injury Nobody Could Know
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The chat predicts a varsity player's ACL tear with a timestamp. Marcus, the player's best friend, tries to warn him and is brushed off. When it happens, Marcus realizes he could have stopped it. Beat: guilt as the price of foreknowledge.

chapters.title: What Dominic Recognizes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The predictions' language mirrors phrases from the school board's sealed meeting minutes — documents Dominic has only seen redacted. Someone is feeding the chat. Beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks the Rule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo screenshots the chat and shows a teacher, hoping an adult will fix it. Within a day the prediction engine turns personal, forecasting Theo's suspension for a vandalism he didn't commit. Beat: the cost of trusting the system.

chapters.title: June's Archive
chapters.summary: June's POV. The school newspaper's editor digs into the board's buried scandal: a decade-old hazing cover-up the winning streak was built to distract from. June and Dominic compare notes and realize their evidence is two halves of one story. Beat: alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Prediction That Names Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat's latest message: 'One of you leaves before spring break.' Wren, already an outsider, assumes it means them and starts withdrawing. Dominic catches them shredding their notes. Beat: fear turning the group inward.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Coach Voss reveals he knows about the flash drive and offers Dominic a full ride in exchange for silence and the originals. Dominic, who has never been offered anything, says they'll think about it. Beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: Marcus Confesses
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus admits he was the one who leaked the board minutes to the chat — his brother works in the district office — but insists he never wrote the predictions. Someone else is curating. Beat: loyalty fracturing under suspicion.

chapters.title: The Night of the Fire Drill That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A prediction promises a real fire in the gym during the semifinal. The six split: warn the school and expose themselves, or stay silent and risk lives. They trigger an anonymous alarm; the gym evacuates before a wiring fault sparks. Beat: collective courage, first taste of acting together.

chapters.title: Spring Break, Missing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren doesn't come back from break. Their family won't answer; the school calls it a transfer. The chat goes dark for the first time. Beat: grief and the horrible confirmation that predictions come true.

chapters.title: Reading the Redactions
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic and June reconstruct the sealed minutes from fragments: the hazing victim was Wren's older sibling, and the board paid the family to leave town. Wren wasn't random — they were the point. Beat: the buried past surfacing.

chapters.title: The Curator
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Tracing the chat's metadata, Theo finds the account belongs to a district IT contractor — the same person who redacted the minutes and now wants the story finished, using the six as leverage against the board. Beat: the puppeteer revealed, but not stopped.

chapters.title: Dominic's Choice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Voss escalates: publish and the scholarship dies, stay and the streak — and the cover-up — survives another decade. Dominic spends a sleepless night with three years of careful spread across the floor. Beat: identity crisis; who is Dominic without the invisibility?

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The five remaining meet in the newspaper room. June argues for immediate publication; Marcus for going to the board first; Theo wants out entirely. They vote: publish, but only with Wren's story told fully and fairly. Beat: loyalty redefined as truth-telling together.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: June's POV. Production night. The district's lawyers threaten injunctions; the contractor's final prediction arrives — 'The story dies Friday' — and the printer mysteriously cancels. June, Dominic, and Marcus hand-deliver copies at dawn. Beat: exhaustion, defiance, no guarantees.

chapters.title: The Streak Ends
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The exposé runs; the semifinal is forfeited mid-investigation; Voss resigns without a word to Dominic. Marcus watches his best friend's college dreams dissolve and feels both ruin and relief. Beat: the price of survival paid in public.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried, Unburied
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. State investigators arrive; the hazing cover-up becomes statewide news; the contractor is arrested but the predictions' source remains half-explained — a leak inside the district that may never be fully known. Beat: justice, incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns, having been moved by their family to escape the story, and reads the article that told their sibling's name with dignity. They rejoin the group not as a prediction but as a person. Beat: grief met with belonging.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Question
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The scholarship is revoked; a stranger who read the story quietly endows a new one in the victim's name, and the committee offers it to Dominic. Dominic accepts — not as a reward for silence, but for speaking. Beat: identity rebuilt on truth instead of carefulness.

chapters.title: Worth It
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Graduation-adjacent spring. The chat's last standing prediction expires unfulfilled; the six archive it for good. On the bleachers where Dominic once kept silent score, they keep honest ones now. Final message in the chat: 'worth it.' Beat: bittersweet resolution — the price was paid, and it was worth it.
